text:
maria: Heads up — saw a cluster of 95th/99th tail spikes in eu-west last night around 23:12 UTC. traceroutes point to a burst of host-level heartbeat processing during warmup that correlates with increased request handling time.
ken: can you paste the agent snippet?
maria: snippet: ```
[2026-03-20T23:12:04Z] host=eu-west-3a heartbeat_fanout=284 queued_replies=12
[2026-03-20T23:12:04Z] host=eu-west-3a kv_cache_regen=1 heatup_workers=6
```
ravi: 284 is way above normal. we typically see <40 on warmups. smells like stale signal or an extra scheduled fanout loop.
liz: did that affect any reserved/dedicated pools or only multi-tenant hosts?
maria: mostly shared pools. one dedicated fallback request got routed while the host was spiky and experienced ~180ms additional tail.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: agent v2.14.3 rolled at 22:50 UTC, no deploy failures reported.
ken: our router doesn't currently consider heartbeat_fanout when picking hosts. we surface it in host metrics but not in routing decisions; so noisy warmups can attract traffic before the host cools down.
ravi: proposed mitigation: soft-affinity guardrail in router. rule: avoid routing high-qps shared tenants to hosts with recent heartbeat_fanout > 100 for 30s. also emit per-tenant inferred_throttle metric so we detect cross-tenant impact earlier.
liz: tradeoffs? reserving headroom or adding routing constraints will reduce packing efficiency.
ken: quick back-of-envelope: reserving ~5% headroom per AZ or adding micro reserved pools increases monthly GPU cost ~2-4%, but should cut those tail incidents and reduce oncall churn.
maria: alternate: small dedicated micro-pool for bursty customers (fast warmup isolation). pros: clean isolation for critical tenants. cons: utilization loss and commitment management.
ravi: router pseudo: ```
if host.heartbeat_fanout_recent > 100 or host.kv_cache_regen_rate > 0.5:
  prefer_hosts = find_hosts(lambda h: h.fanout_recent < 20 and h.kv_cache_regen_rate < 0.1)
  if not prefer_hosts and tenant.priority != "high":
    backoff_or_queue_request()
```
ken: We need index+TTL on heartbeat_fanout_recent in the host metric store (TTL 60s) and expose it to the decision cache for low-cost reads.
liz: ops checklist: 1) add metric + TTL 2) add router rule behind FF 3) canary in eu-west 4) dashboard with per-tenant inferred_throttle and host_fanout.
maria: I'll own metric + dashboard. ken, can you implement the FFed router rule and run a canary in eu-west-3 tomorrow morning?
ken: yes. I'll post the canary playbook and expected SLO impact.
ravi: i'll run cost sims: 5% headroom vs 10-node micro-pool using last quarter's traffic traces to estimate utilization loss and false-positive routing.
liz: add runbook note: if heartbeat_fanout > 200 for >1min, oncall should consider quarantining the host and temporarily draining new allocations.
maria: also suggest alert: inferred_throttle_ratio_by_tenant > 0.03 for 5m -> page infra-sre.
ops-bot: infra-monitor: draft alert created for inferred_throttle_ratio_by_tenant (threshold=0.03, window=5m).
ken: thanks. will update here with canary results and routing rule diff.
maria: thanks everyone 0:30. we'll reconvene in the morning sync. :thumbsup:
